name: Abell 399, hostless supernova field (Hubble)
blurb: Abell 399, a rich galaxy cluster, seen by Hubble at the site of an apparently hostless supernova.
label: abell3993140-hubble
story: Somewhere in this patch of the galaxy cluster Abell 399, a Type Ia supernova once flared and faded with no galaxy in sight. Hubble stared deep at the spot to learn whether the star belonged to a hidden faint host or to the stars that drift between the cluster's galaxies.

claims.text: Abell 399 is one of four rich galaxy clusters targeted for apparently hostless Type Ia supernovae
The supernova Abell399_3_14_0 (from MENeaCS) is a normal Type Ia
Deep Hubble imaging was taken at the locations of potentially hostless, long-faded Type Ia supernovae
The goal was to test whether such supernovae belong to the intracluster stellar population rather than a faint host
